rules.statement: A donor under Kandyan Law has the right to cancel or revoke any gift unilaterally by an instrument in writing without the consent of the donee or other interested parties.
rules.supporting_quote: (1) Kandyan Law gives the right to a donor without the consent of the donee or any other person, such as the life interest holder, to cancel or revoke any gift by an instrument in writing in conformity with the law. (2) However, gifts to a temple, gifts in consideration of marriage, gifts effecting a charitable trust and gifts where right to revoke is renounced s. 8 (1) (d) are the exceptions. (3) Although the donor explained in the deed of gift that he was giving a gift which was irrevocable and absolute under all circumstances, he did not say that he was renouncing his right to revoke such an "irrevocable and absolute" gift. The section expected such renunciation in words similar to what is mentioned in s. 5 (1) (a), if a gift was to be considered as an exception to the general rule of revocability of gifts under the Kandyan Law. 348

rules.statement: A gift to a temple, in consideration of marriage, effecting a charitable trust, or where the right to revoke is renounced, falls within section 8.

rules.statement: A donor's declaration of an irrevocable and absolute gift does not necessarily constitute a renunciation of the right to revoke unless expressed in words similar to those mentioned in section 5.
